purpose: The ways a running kotlin program can HOLD layer-1 content. Not layer 1 (the data is fixed), not layer 3 (no operations beyond load-and-read-back), not the type system.
reference: language knowledge, checked against ../type_vocabulary/raw/kotlin.types.json as a candidate checklist only (superseded node; not a decision instrument).

nothing.note: the absence value; any nullable type can hold it.
a value carrying nothing, the single-inhabitant shape returned by statements; this is a full value, not an absence, unlike the null probe above.
the bottom type; the only value it can ever hold is null itself, so this rep is inhabited by exactly the absence probe and nothing else.

whole.note: signed 32-bit; the default whole-number holder, refuses anything past its own width at compile time.
signed 64-bit; reaches i64max cleanly, refuses i64max_plus1 and u64max at compile time.
unsigned 64-bit; the one whole-holder built to take u64max cleanly, refuses anything below zero.
arbitrary-width whole number built from digit text; every edge in the data file fits with room to spare.

fractional.note: IEEE double, the default fractional holder.
IEEE single; holds every base value but silently loses precision on the wide whole edges if reused there, and rounds pi to fewer digits.
arbitrary-precision decimal text with no concept of NaN or Infinity; the special-value probes are natural attempts that throw at run time rather than construct anything.

text.note: immutable utf-16 text, the default text holder.
a mutable run of utf-16 code units; the clef codepoint sits across two elements, not one.
a mutable text buffer built by appending onto the base text.
holds text only as encoded utf-8 bytes; the codepoints are gone until decoded back.

sequence.note: a read-only ordered run built by a factory function, one declared element kind.

probes.mixed: val v: List<Any?> = listOf(1, "two", 3.0, true, null)

sequence.note: the same ordered run but open to in-place add, remove, and set after it is built.

probes.mixed: val v: MutableList<Any?> = mutableListOf(1, "two", 3.0, true, null)

sequence.note: a fixed-length run backed by a raw array, element kind fixed by the declared type parameter.

probes.mixed: val v: Array<Any?> = arrayOf(1, "two", 3.0, true, null)

sequence.note: a specialized primitive-element array with no boxing; the narrowest sequence holder, refuses non-numeric elements outright.

probes.mixed: val v: IntArray = intArrayOf(1, "two", 3.0, true, null)

sequence.note: an ordered run open to push and pop at both ends.

probes.mixed: val v: ArrayDeque<Any?> = ArrayDeque(listOf(1, "two", 3.0, true, null))

keyed.note: a read-only name-to-element grouping built by a factory function, insertion order kept for iteration.

probes.flat: val v: Map<String, Long> = mapOf("a" to 1, "b" to 2, "c" to 3)
probes.intlike: val v: Map<String, String> = mapOf("1" to "string-one-key", "b" to "2")
probes.emptykey: val v: Map<String, String> = mapOf("" to "empty-string key")
probes.nested: val v: Map<String, Map<String, List<Long>>> = mapOf("outer" to mapOf("inner" to listOf(1, 2)))

keyed.note: the same grouping open to in-place put and remove after it is built.

probes.flat: val v: MutableMap<String, Long> = mutableMapOf("a" to 1, "b" to 2, "c" to 3)
probes.intlike: val v: MutableMap<String, String> = mutableMapOf("1" to "string-one-key", "b" to "2")
probes.emptykey: val v: MutableMap<String, String> = mutableMapOf("" to "empty-string key")
probes.nested: val v: MutableMap<String, MutableMap<String, MutableList<Long>>> = mutableMapOf("outer" to mutableMapOf("inner" to mutableListOf(1, 2)))

keyed.note: the concrete class behind Kotlin's default map factories, named directly rather than through a factory function; insertion order kept explicitly.

probes.flat: val v = LinkedHashMap<String, Long>(); v["a"] = 1; v["b"] = 2; v["c"] = 3
probes.intlike: val v = LinkedHashMap<String, String>(); v["1"] = "string-one-key"; v["b"] = "2"
probes.emptykey: val v = LinkedHashMap<String, String>(); v[""] = "empty-string key"
probes.nested: val v = LinkedHashMap<String, LinkedHashMap<String, List<Long>>>(); val inner = LinkedHashMap<String, List<Long>>(); inner["inner"] = listOf(1, 2); v["outer"] = inner

keyed.spelling: data class R3(val a: Long, val b: Long, val c: Long)
keyed.note: field names are fixed when the shape is written, not when the data arrives; the odd keys are not spellable as field names at all.

probes.flat:
data class R3(val a: Long, val b: Long, val c: Long)
val v = R3(1, 2, 3)
probes.intlike:
data class RI(val `1`: Long, val b: String)
val v = RI(1, "2")
probes.emptykey:
data class RE(val `` : String)
val v = RE("empty-string key")
probes.nested:
data class RN(val outer: List<Long>)
val v = RN(listOf(1, 2))

nesting.note: nesting by repeating the same holder; the element type parameter must widen to Any? once depth or form varies within one run.

probes.seq_in_map: val v: Map<String, Map<String, List<Long>>> = mapOf("outer" to mapOf("inner" to listOf(1, 2)))
probes.mixed_depth: val v: List<Any?> = listOf(1, listOf(2, mapOf("k" to "t")), true, null)

nesting.spelling: sealed class Node; class Whole(val n: Long): Node(); class Seq(val items: List<Node>): Node() ...
nesting.pre:
sealed class Node
data class NNull(val u: Unit = Unit): Node()
data class NTruth(val b: Boolean): Node()
data class NWhole(val n: Long): Node()
data class NText(val s: String): Node()
data class NSeq(val items: List<Node>): Node()
data class NMap(val entries: Map<String, Node>): Node()
nesting.note: a hand-written sum shape; the only kotlin holder here that takes every layer-1 form in one element position, which is what mixed-depth nesting needs.

probes.seq_in_seq: val v: Node = NSeq(listOf(NSeq(listOf(NWhole(1), NWhole(2))), NSeq(listOf(NWhole(3), NWhole(4)))))
probes.seq_in_map: val v: Node = NMap(mapOf("outer" to NMap(mapOf("inner" to NSeq(listOf(NWhole(1), NWhole(2)))))))
probes.mixed_depth: val v: Node = NSeq(listOf(NWhole(1), NSeq(listOf(NWhole(2), NMap(mapOf("k" to NText("t"))))), NTruth(true), NNull()))

identity.note: a mutable holder passed by reference; putting the same object in two positions makes both positions name one node, so a mutation through one is visible through the other.

probes.shared:
val s: MutableList<Long> = mutableListOf(1, 2, 3)
val v: MutableList<MutableList<Long>> = mutableListOf(s, s)
v[0].add(99)
val r: String = if (v[1].last() == 99L) "shared" else "copied"
probes.diamond:
val t: MutableList<Long> = mutableListOf(7)
val v: List<MutableList<Long>> = listOf(t, t)
val r: String = if (v[0] === v[1]) "same" else "distinct"
probes.cycle:
val v: MutableList<Any?> = mutableListOf()
v.add(v)
val r: String = if (v[0] === v) "cycle" else "no-cycle"

identity.note: a named shape whose field holds a reference to a sub-node; two boxes built from the same list co-node the one list.

probes.shared:
data class Box(val items: MutableList<Long>)
val s: MutableList<Long> = mutableListOf(1, 2, 3)
val left = Box(s)
val right = Box(s)
left.items.add(99)
val r: String = if (right.items.last() == 99L) "shared" else "copied"
probes.diamond:
data class Box(val items: MutableList<Long>)
val t: MutableList<Long> = mutableListOf(7)
val viaA = Box(t)
val viaB = Box(t)
val r: String = if (viaA.items === viaB.items) "same" else "distinct"
probes.cycle:
class Node(var name: String) { var selfref: Node? = null }
val n = Node("loop")
n.selfref = n
val r: String = if (n.selfref === n) "cycle" else "no-cycle"

identity.spelling: data class Point(val x: Long, val y: Long); p.copy()
identity.note: a shape holding only primitive fields, so copying it copies the values rather than sharing a sub-node; mutation is impossible since the fields are val, but a fresh copy still starts equal-by-content and independent, which is the value-copying case rather than a reference-sharing one.

probes.shared:
data class Point(val x: Long, val y: Long)
val s = Point(1, 2)
val left = s.copy()
val right = s.copy()
val r: String = if (left == right && left !== right) "copied" else "shared"
probes.diamond:
data class Point(val x: Long, val y: Long)
val t = Point(7, 7)
val viaA = t.copy()
val viaB = t.copy()
val r: String = if (viaA === viaB) "same" else "distinct"
probes.cycle:
data class Point(val x: Long, val self: Point)
val n = Point(1, Point(2, Point(3, Point(4, null!!))))
val r: String = if (n.self.self === n) "cycle" else "no-cycle"
